*FITCHBURG CITY CLERK, Oct 28 2026 2:02 pm*

# August 25, 2026 10:04 a.m. - Monthly Retirement Board Meeting

The regular meeting of the Fitchburg Retirement Board was called to order by Chairperson Thomas Dateo Jr. on August 25, 2026, at 10:04 a.m., in the North Meeting Room of Fitchburg City Hall, located at 718 Main Street, Fitchburg, MA 01420.

Fitchburg Retirement Board members present: Thomas Dateo Jr. (Chair), John Brown, Mary Cringan, Jacquelyn Cronin and Anna Farrell.

Staff present: Director Steffani Santiago and Assistant Director Geraldine Conley.

Public present: Laura Strickland, PRIT Senior Client Services Officer

### Review and Accept Election Certification for Elected Member Position:

Ms. Santiago noted for the record that the Notice of Election for the Board's Third Member Elected Position was posted and circulated on June 30, 2026, and that Nominations closed on August 17, 2026. Only one candidate pulled and returned Nomination Papers. Incumbent Anna Farrell's Nomination Papers were certified on July 1, 2026. On a motion made by Mary Cringan and seconded by John Brown to declare Anna Farrell to be elected as the Third Member of the Fitchburg Retirement Board for a term to expire October 31, 2029. Voted unanimously (5-0). Mr. Dateo Jr. congratulted Ms. Farrell and thanked her for continuing to serve the members of the System.

### Review and accept Financial Statement, Required Supplementary Information, and Audit of Specific Elements for CY24 as prepared by City's outside auditing firm CBIZ:

The Board reviewed the Financial Statement Required Supplementary Information and Audit of Specific Elements for CY24. Ms. Santiago reviewed the audit findings and the auditor's suggestion to send out letters for all deceased retirees with an outstanding balance due regardless of the amount of money owed. On a motion made by Anna Farrell and seconded by John Brown to accept the Financial Statement, Required Supplementary Information and Audit of Specific Elements for CY24. Voted unanimously (5-0).

### Review and Approval of the Cash Disbursements Warrant:

The Board reviewed the August 2026 Cash Disbursements Warrant totaling $32,016.28. On a motion made by Mary Cringan and seconded by Jacquelyn Cronin, to approve the August 2026 Cash Disbursements Warrant. Voted unanimously (5-0).

### Review and Approval of the Refunds/Rollovers/Transfers Warrant:

The Board reviewed the August 2026 Refunds/Rollovers/Transfers Warrant totaling $124,335.98. On a motion made by John Brown and seconded by Jacquelyn Cronin, to approve the August 2026 Refunds/Rollovers/Transfers Warrant. Voted unanimously (5-0).

### Review and Approve June 23, 2026 and July 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes:

The Board reviewed the June 23, 2026 and July 28, 2026 meeting minutes. On a motion made by Anna Farrell and seconded by Mary Cringan, to approve the June 23, 2026 and July 28, 2026 Meeting Minutes. Voted unanimously (5 -0).

---

### Review and Approval of Cashbooks:

The Board reviewed the Cashbooks for December 31, 2025, January 31, 2026, February 28, 2026 and March 31, 2026. On a motion made by Mary Cringan and seconded by Anna Farrell to accept the Cashbooks for December 31, 2025, January 31, 2026, February 28, 2026 and March 31, 2026. Voted unanimously (5-0).

### Prim Annual Update:

Laura Strickland, Senior Client Services Officer joined the meeting at 10:12 a.m., to provide an annual update as of June 30, 2026 of the System's portfolio. The Fitchburg Retirement System is fully invested with the PRTIT Fund. The funds are overseen by nine (9) member Board of Trustees, five (5) advisory committees and a staff of approximately 60 professionals. Each individual asset class has its own dedicated investment team. PRIT's Risk and Research leaders reviews and rebalances investments on a monthly basis. PRIT is one of the leanest pension investment firm systems in the country. There are two newly elected Board members, Matthew Scheffler, State Teacher's Retirement and Joseph Connarton, State Employees' Retirement. Ms. Strickland reported that the PRIT Fund is at a record high. The Fitchburg Retirement System General Allocation funds are preforming well. No change in Asset Allocations recommended. The Board thanked Ms. Strickland for providing them with an update on the System's investment portfolio. Ms. Strickland left the meeting at 10:48 a.m.

### Review and Accept of Bank Statements:

The Board reviewed the Bank Statements for December 31, 2025, January 31, 2026. February 28, 2026 and March 31, 2026. On a motion made by Thomas Dateo Jr. and seconded by John Brown to accept the Bank Statements for December 31, 20225, January 31, 2026, February 28, 2026 and March 31, 2026 subject to City Auditor Approval. Voted unanimously (5-0).

### Review and Approval of Retirement Applications:

**Michael R. Chandler,** Police Officer, Superannuation Retirement Allowance, Option C, effective August 1, 2026. On a motion made by John Brown and seconded by Mary Cringan, to approve Michael R. Chandler's Option C, Superannuation Retirement effective August 1, 2026. Voted unanimously (5-0).

**Alexander Rodriguez,** School Department Paraprofessional, Superannuation Retirement Allowance, Option C, effective August 1, 2026. On a motion made by Mary Cringan and seconded by Anna Farrell, to approve Alexander Rodriguez's Option C, Superannuation Retirement effective August 1, 2026. Voted unanimously (5-0).

### Discussion regarding Webster First Deduction for Retirees:

Ms. Santiago informed the Board historically, when Webster First maintained an office within City Hall, employees and retirees could elect to have funds directed to Webster First through a payroll deduction. These deductions are currently combined into a single vendor check accompanied by a ledger identifying the amount attributable to each individual. Webster First must then retrieve the check and manually allocate the funds to the appropriate accounts. Because Webster First no longer maintains an office within City Hall, this process is outdated and administratively inefficient. The Retirement Office has contacted affected retirees over the years and requested that they complete a direct deposit form authorizing Webster First as a secondary ACH deposit. All but three retirees have transitioned to this process.

Webster First has requested that the remaining accounts be converted to electronic deposits or, alternatively, that Retirement Office staff deliver the vendor check directly to the credit union. Ms. Santiago recommended that the remaining retirees be notified that the Retirement System will discontinue the Webster First payroll-deduction arrangement effective on a specified date. To continue having a portion of their monthly benefit deposited with Webster First, they must submit a completed direct deposit authorization establishing Webster First as a secondary deposit account by the stated deadline. If the required authorization is not received, no further Webster First deduction will be withheld. The retiree's full net monthly benefit will instead be deposited into the primary bank account currently on file with the Retirement System.

On a motion made by John Brown and seconded by Jacquelyn Cronin, to notifying the effected retirees that the Retirement Office will be discontinuing the Webster First payroll-deduction arrangement effective two months from notification. If retirees with to establish a secondary depository they must complete and return a direct deposit form. If the required authorization is not received, no further Webster First deduction will be withheld and the full net monthly benefit will instead be deposited into the primary bank account on file. Voted unanimously (5-0).

### Legislative Updates

**_Review Draft updated Guidelines for Vacation & PTO Buybacks_** – Ms. Santiago circulated an updated draft of the guidelines discussed by the Board during its June 23, 2026 meeting. Mr. Dateo Jr., requested members review the material for further discussion at the September meeting. On a motion made by Mary Cringan and seconded by John Brown, to table the discussion of the draft supplemental regulation changes for Vacation and PTO Buybacks to the September Meeting. Voted unanimously (5-0).

### Director/Assistant Director Communications (Pending/Tabled Matters):

**_Discuss Attorney Gibson's 08/18/26 email correspondence regarding accounts payable practices_** – The Board reviewed and briefly discussed.

**_PERAC Administrator Training_ -** Ms. Santiago advised the Board that the Retirement Staff did not attend the training in Northampton due to the current workload, but planned to attend the next seminar in Norwood.

**_Actuarial Valuation Update_** – Ms. Santiago is working on finalizing all request and has corresponded with John Boorack. Based on the records identified, it appears there may have been a glitch when the Board transition to PTG in 2009 as many records as listing conflicting benefit information that do not tie out to the actual payment records. To ensure the actuary has the correct data to complete the valuation and to update records contained in Baystate, each of the identified, Ms. Santiago has had to audit over 50 retiree files.

**_Baystate Electronic Onboarding rollout update_** – Ms. Santiago advised the Board that the City HR Department is using the electronic onboarding platform for eligible new employees to enroll with the Retirement System. She has worked closely with Baystate representatives to continue to develop the module as the goal is to establish the practice across all member units. Once the final development requests have been released to production, retirement staff will work with HR representative in the School Department, Housing Authority, and Redevelopment Authority.

**_School Department PBS/Daily Subs_** – Ms. Santiago advised the Board that she was notified via email from the School Department's HR Office on August 11, 2026 that they had eliminated the Permanent Building Substitute (PBS) positions effective the end of the 25/26 school year. As full-time PBS were scheduled to work 20 hours per week for 35 weeks or more, employees hired into said position were eligible for membership with the Retirement System. The email correspondence received inquired where these members should contribute if they moved into Daily Substitute positions (Daily Subs). Daily Subs are part time/per diem employees with no set or regular schedule.

Ms. Santiago advised that she reviewed the members identified in the email correspondence and noted some of the employees were not enrolled as members in the Retirement System. Ms. Santiago request a copy of the job description. The School's HR Director Cari Fabale followed up via phone and explained that PBS were notified their positions were being eliminated and thus they would no longer be employed by the district. Employees were given the option to apply for and be rehired as Daily Subs. Ms. Santiago informed Ms. Fabale if employees were terminated at the end of the school year and later rehired for the next school year in positions that did not meet eligibility requirements for membership with the retirement system, that said employees would have to contribute to OBRA. Ms. Santiago advised if any employees were simply transitioned from PBS to Daily Subs, they would maintain membership rights and would continue to contribute to the Fitchburg Retirement System. Ms. Fabale advised that eight (8) of the ten (10) PBS were termed as of 6/26/26 and rehired as Daily Subs as of 8/25/26. Two (2) of the PBS were transferred to the Daily Sub positions. Ms. Santiago informed Ms. Fabale that the two employees who transferred to Daily Sub did not experience a break in service and therefore maintained membership rights and would need to continue to contribute to the Retirement System.

**PRIT Fund Update:** The Board reviewed and briefly discussed the PRIT Fund Performance Summary and Participant Statement for July 31, 2026 and the PRIM Board 2026 2nd Quarter Update.

**PERAC Memos:** None

### Accidental Disability Retirement Application(s):

**_Michael Smith_ –** Ms. Santiago advised the Board that she had received the requested medical documentation from Mr. Smith providers. The records were provided to and reviewed by Attorney Gibson. Attorney Gibson advised that the correspondence provided met prima facie requirements for acceptance by the Board to vote to convene a medical panel. On a motion made by John Brown and seconded by Anna Farrell, to submit the required documents to PERAC and request a medical panel be convened for Michael Smith. Voted unanimously (5-0).
